app.title: OPTIMEO: design of experiments, Bayesian optimization and response modelling
app.summary: The person first plans a set of experimental runs: they describe each process parameter by its type and range, pick a design type (a filterable guide helps), and download the run table with an empty response column. Once the runs have results, they load the table, correct cells, choose which columns are parameters and which are outcomes, and set each parameter's type and allowed range. They mark each outcome as maximize, minimize or constraint-only, add fixed parameters, linear constraints and an exploration setting, then fit a surrogate model. The model proposes the next batch of experiments and the best settings so far. They can inspect the model through 2D slices, an optimization trace, a sensitivity analysis and Pareto fronts, predict outcomes at chosen settings, or fit linear and machine-learning regression models to see which factors matter.

task.text: Choose which experiments to run next, from a planned design and the results so far, so a process reaches its best settings in as few runs as possible.

data.text: A tidy table of experimental runs: process parameters (continuous, integer or categorical) in some columns, and one or more measured outcomes in the others.
data.item: one experimental run: a setting of each process parameter, plus its measured outcomes

stage.text: planning and steering rounds of process experiments, between batches of runs

mechanism.text: Three tabbed pages share one tidy-table input. The design page turns a parameter form into a run table that can be downloaded. The optimization page turns an editable results table and goal settings into a fitted model, then shows next-run and best-so-far tables, model slices, trace, sensitivity and Pareto plots. The analysis page runs diagnostic plots and linear or machine-learning fits, each with a what-if prediction form.

field.text: design of experiments and Bayesian optimization for tuning an experimental process

workflow.name: plan the next batch of experiments from a model of the results so far

steps.step: lay out an initial set of runs to cover the parameter space
steps.here: a filterable guide suggests designs by factor count, factor type, expected relationships and purpose. The person then sets parameter names, types, low/high/intermediate values and design options (Sobol, factorial, Latin hypercube, Box-Behnken, central composite and others), with optional linear constraints. The run table and its pair plots are drawn, and the design downloads as CSV or XLSX with an empty response column

a CSV or Excel results table is uploaded, column names are cleaned, and cells can be edited and rows added or deleted in place. Parameter and outcome columns are picked, and each parameter gets a type and a min/max range, or an allow-list for categorical parameters

steps.step: set the goal and the limits of the search
steps.here: each outcome is set to maximize, minimize or 'not an objective'. The person also sets the number of new runs, fixed parameters with their values, linear parameter and outcome constraints, and an optional exploit/balanced/explore UCB beta

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: 'Compute / Update model' fits the Gaussian-process model and lists the next experiments to perform, with predicted outcomes, beside the best parameters found so far. The button stays disabled until a setting changes

steps.step: check what the model has learned
steps.here: optional slice values fix extra parameters for 2D contour plots of each objective. An optimization trace, a per-objective sensitivity analysis and, for several objectives, Pareto fronts with or without error bars are also shown. A predictions tab gives the predicted mean ± standard error at chosen settings

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: on the analysis page: Q-Q plot, box plot, histogram, correlation and pair plots, a Pareto chart of standardized effects at a chosen α, and per-factor polynomial fits. These are followed by an editable statsmodels formula fit and a choice of six scikit-learn models, each with a prediction form
each optimization plot downloads as Plotly JSON with a commented Python loader. The design table downloads as CSV/XLSX

distinctive: up to ten outcomes, any of which can be objectives (maximize or minimize) while the rest act as linear constraints, with Pareto fronts drawn when there are several objectives
the search can be bounded by fixed parameters (for runs done in parallel at one shared setting) and by linear inequality or equality constraints on parameters
parameter ranges can be widened beyond the measured values so the optimizer can propose settings outside what has been tried
an exploration–exploitation control (UCB beta with Exploit/Balanced/Explore presets) switches between single and batch acquisition depending on how many runs are requested
the planned design is exported with an empty response column, so it comes back as the results table for the optimization step
